name: Euler Finance
tldr: A little-used donate function let users reduce their own collateral without checking if the position was still healthy.
what: Euler was a large, well-audited lending protocol: deposit collateral, borrow against it.
happened: Using flash loans, the attacker donated collateral to the reserves to make his own position insolvent on purpose, then liquidated himself at a discount and walked away with the difference.
bug: donateToReserves did not run the same health check as every other function that touches collateral.
prevent: Every new function must preserve the core invariant: a position can never end up with more debt than collateral.
lesson: One overlooked edge case can sink a battle-tested protocol. New functions deserve the same scrutiny as the old ones.

sources.title: Mixin Network - REKT (notes Euler's funds were returned)
